scope: Pairwise audit of 12 named theory modules at their current declared claim ceilings. A non-conflict classification is not a proof of empirical truth, a bridge, equality, joint-state existence, or higher-order consistency.

relation_vocabulary.compatible: The two typed claims are directly co-satisfiable in their already-declared matched scope. This does not assert identity or mutual implication.
relation_vocabulary.conditional-on-common-carrier-or-map: No conflict follows once an explicit common carrier, common lift, typed map, response map, or commutation contract is supplied; composition is not licensed without it.
relation_vocabulary.orthogonal-estimand: The modules estimate or constrain different typed objects, so their claims are not logical negations and no automatic composition is implied.
relation_vocabulary.open-bridge: No current contradiction is identified, but the scientifically useful cross-layer identification or composition remains unproved at the stated generality.
relation_vocabulary.actual-conflict: The modules make jointly unsatisfiable claims after carrier, types, scope, and estimand have been matched.

modules.estimand: admissible causal set and next-observation learning value
declared simulator dynamics and complete-state sufficiency
warning-blind loss conditioning, within-domain warning, and portability bounds
revision after compression and revision debt

pairs.rationale: CCOC future obstruction can refine a CREST required state when both act on one declared carrier; absent that match it is not a contradiction.
MLTR transport or repair contributes to a joint required state only through a declared common lift or typed replacement map.
MRM mechanism-response distinctions enter a CREST contract only after candidate mechanisms and responses are typed on a common carrier.
CREST asks which distinctions are structurally required; CED asks which required distinctions or targets current evidence licenses.
A required-state quotient and an evidence-conditioned admissible causal set are different typed objects with different objectives.
A bounded two-world eco-genetic bridge exists, but no full simulator-domain equality between CompleteSimulatorState and CREST RequiredState is established.
Empirical warning coordinates do not yet identify a complete natural CREST state; the empirical warning-state bridge remains open.
CREST adequacy under C0 and TU-1 failure of later reuse under C1 are co-satisfiable; TU-1 is the exact same-carrier reuse specialization plus repair cost.
Exact structural adequacy and graded causal-learning or report-licensing utility answer different questions.
The TU-3 loss quotient agrees with loss-specialized CREST only when the full loss signature exhausts the CREST responsibilities on the same carrier.
TU-4 is a CREST-style joint responsibility once loss and warning responses are defined on the same declared model-world carrier.
Future and history obstructions can join without conflict on a common carrier or lift, but neither supplies the other's transport map.
Future and mechanism closures are co-satisfiable joint responsibilities after their response domains are aligned.
A future-grammar obstruction is structural, whereas CED concerns evidence compatibility and reporting.
Opening a future grammar and selecting an observation for causal learning have distinct estimands.
Simulator futures could instantiate a CCOC grammar, but no general source-faithful grammar map from EGC is registered.
Warning-domain futures and CCOC composition futures have no completed typed bridge at their current generality.
A CCOC future opening can instantiate the C0-to-C1 revision in TU-1 only after old and revised states are placed on a common carrier.
Future obstruction does not rank causal-learning observations or license a report target.
Mapping a changed future grammar into a contract-complete loss-response signature is a plausible but unproved bridge.
Future-interface obstruction and warning-versus-loss refinement can both hold without being the same claim.
History transport and mechanism robustness can be jointly audited when replacement and mechanism maps share a carrier or common lift.
Declared historical meaning and evidence-qualified reportability are different estimands.
History transport does not identify a causal programme, and causal admissibility does not supply an inherited semantic map.
A simulator history could provide an MLTR carrier, but no general history/replacement projection from EGC is completed.
Historical replacement and warning portability are related transport problems, but their cross-domain semantic bridge remains open.
TU-1 is same-carrier revision; the carrier-changing revision needed to subsume MLTR transport is explicitly open.
Semantic/history transport and experiment utility do not estimate the same object.
TU-3 representation faithfulness is same-carrier, while MLTR may change carriers; a lift-invariant loss map is not proved.
Connecting historical transport to warning portability requires a declared cross-state correspondence and commutation result not yet supplied.
The positive bridge composes MRM response classes with CED licensing on finite shared bridge worlds; it does not create a canonical natural embedding.
The positive bridge maps RACH-admissible programmes to MRM response classes under one declared action/target carrier.
EGC mechanisms or state coordinates require an explicit schema map before they become an MRM candidate-law family.
No general map currently shows which eco-genetic warning differences are mechanism-relevant MRM response distinctions.
TU-1 can audit a changed mechanism responsibility only when old and revised MRM states share a carrier or typed lift.
Mechanism-safe response equivalence is neither causal-learning value nor target-licensing status.
MRM distinctions enter TU-3 only when retained mechanism responsibilities are included in the full loss-response signature.
A general mechanism-to-warning response bridge is not established even though both can coexist on a declared carrier.
The finite positive bridge keeps causal multiplicity while licensing a target on shared evidence-compatible bridge worlds.
Simulator output does not become reliability-qualified evidence about nature without an empirical observation and calibration bridge.
The empirical warning programme requires an explicit CED reliability/reportability projection before generic evidence licensing follows.
Reportability under current evidence and revisability after stored compression are different axes.
TU-2 preserves CED target licensing as a distinct utility and proves that RACH learning need not rank it the same way.
Evidence licensing and loss-representation factorization are independent unless an empirical bridge is added.
Mathematical warning-state adequacy does not yet imply empirical identification or CED-licensed portability.
EGC-generated mechanisms can enter RACH only through a declared model-family and observation map not completed here.
Warning observations do not automatically define a RACH causal-programme family or NOV objective.
Causal-set learning and later state revision answer different scientific responsibilities.
TU-2 uses RACH causal-learning utility on its graded branch while explicitly preserving the separation from target licensing.
Causal-learning value and loss-representation faithfulness are distinct estimands.
Admissible causal uncertainty and warning/loss response refinement can vary independently.
EGW can condition on an EGC-derived frozen loss domain when simulator version, endpoints, and observation semantics are explicitly aligned.
Complete simulator-state sufficiency does not by itself answer revision after scientific compression.
Simulator dynamics do not identify a universal experiment ranking between causal learning and report licensing.
TU-3 audits an EGC representation only after the full loss-contract signature and projection are declared on the simulator carrier.
TU-4 can refine an EGC loss domain when loss and warning responses share the declared simulator carrier.
Warning reproducibility or portability does not determine revision debt after an old state was stored.
Warning performance and causal-learning versus report-licensing utility are distinct outcomes.
EGW's warning-blind loss domain corresponds to TU-3 only through a full loss-response and representation map.
TU-4 formalizes EGW's within-state/portability distinction, but empirical application still requires matched loss, warning, and domain semantics.
Revision debt and graded learning/licensing utility are separate additions to the common task-indexed spine.
Both are exact specializations of representation adequacy: one changes the task after storage and the other changes the representation for a fixed loss task.
Reuse after contract change and warning-task refinement are co-satisfiable exact specializations of the task preorder.
TU-2's graded epistemic utility is deliberately a separate branch from TU-3 exact representation adequacy.
Graded causal/report utility and exact loss/warning task refinement are not the same ordering.
TU-3 supplies the contract-complete loss quotient that TU-4 jointly refines with the warning response.
